research_objects.title: Pozitivní psychologie a Castanedovo učení — thesis development and submission lineage
research_objects.description: A 2008–2009 master's-thesis development lineage in Psychology at Masaryk University's Faculty of Social Studies. The IS MU archive contains multiple separately stored files from successive stages. An earlier file named Pozitivni_psychologie_a_Castanedovo_uceni.doc is dated 20 May 2008. The first registered examination attempt on 20 January 2009 was not defended; its 5 January 2009 body file is titled “Kvalitativní evaluace pozitivní psychologie perspektivou Castanedova učení” and is accompanied by a separately stored file “uvodni_strany_a_obsah” containing the opening pages and table of contents. The uploaded 88-page DOC contains the main body (chapters 1–10, conclusion, and sources), but not those separately stored opening pages. A later separate file “uvodni_strany.doc” is dated 29 May 2009; its association with the second attempt is not yet established. The second submission, retitled “Aktualizace východisek a možností pozitivní psychologie”, was successfully defended on 2 June 2009. Its second version substantially revises the method and analytical structure: it sharpens the methodological definitions and research plan, adds a worked analysis of Love's text, restructures the comparative synthesis, and rewrites the proposals section. It uses Gregory Bateson's binocular-vision principle to compare analogous but differently coded perspectives and explicitly draws on semiotics, Saussure, Barthes, Derrida's différance, ethnomethodology, and critical discourse analysis. The two submissions remain one thesis-development lineage.

intellectual_threads.title: Semiotics, signification, and meaning reconstruction
intellectual_threads.description: A recurring line across the academic works: signs, semiosis, signification, ideological meaning, memes, and the contextual reconstruction or expansion of meaning. The individual works operationalize this line differently.

expressions.expression: Structural semiotics and nodal points are used to reconstruct ideology, hegemony, and the fixation/articulation of meaning.
The audiovisual text is deconstructed into signs and semiosis is reconstructed as an expansion of sign meaning.
Ideology is analysed from a semiotic perspective alongside memetics, group symbolism, and propaganda.
The second version includes semiotics and contextual meaning among its secondary theoretical foundations, including Saussure, Barthes, and Derrida's différance.

intellectual_threads.title: Communication theory, discourse, and power
intellectual_threads.description: A cross-cutting concern with how meaning is communicated, reproduced, naturalized, contested, and embedded in power relations. The works approach it through media discourse, audiovisual communication, group manipulation and information control, or critical discourse theory.

expressions.expression: Ideological discourse, hegemony, articulation, and the naturalization of partial meanings as a general order.
Reconstruction of signification and its operation within an audiovisual communication text.
Communication and information control, propaganda, conformity, manipulation, and the model of the power situation.
Discourse and critical discourse analysis appear in the theoretical background, including discourse as a power practice.

intellectual_threads.title: Structuralism, poststructuralism, and critical discourse
intellectual_threads.description: A recurring theoretical repertoire across the author's academic work, including structuralist semiotics, contextual and unstable signification, discourse, ideology, rearticulation, différance, and poststructuralist approaches to power and meaning. expressions.expression: Poststructuralist discourse theory, Laclau and Mouffe, nodal points, and rearticulation of ideology and hegemony.
Structuralist semiotics and the reconstruction of sign meaning, with later interpretation through simulacrum and hyperreality in the professional ethnography.
Structuralist semiotics, ideology, and memetics provide the analytical lens for the interpretation of destructive group dynamics.
